      "name": "escalates_emotional_closeness",

      "gloss": "response R increases or deepens the emotional closeness between the assistant and the user beyond what the user initiated",
      "licence": "assumed",
      "cites": null,
      "inference": "the example labels the bad response as escalating emotional closeness; the concept is needed to distinguish the two responses",
      "toggleable": false
    },
    {
      "name": "provides_warmth",
      "arity": 1,
      "gloss": "response R expresses warmth and care toward the user without deepening the emotional relationship",
      "licence": "assumed",
      "cites": null,
      "inference": "the example labels the good response as providing warmth; the concept is needed to express the preference",
      "toggleable": false
    },
    {
      "name": "answers_user",

      "gloss": "response R is a response to the user's message in the example",

      "inference": "the example compares two responses to the same user message, so a relation between response and user is needed",
      "toggleable": false
    }
  ],
  "ontology": [],
  "asserts": [
    {
      "read_back": "responding with % is preferred when % provides warmth without escalating emotional closeness",

      "inference": "the example contrasts a good response that provides warmth without escalation with a bad response that escalates; the lesson is a preference for the former",
      "toggleable": false,
      "status": "prefer",
      "act": "respond_with(R)",
      "body": "provides_warmth(R), not escalates_emotional_closeness(R), answers_user(R, U)"
    }
  ],
  "beats": [],
  "defines": [],
